summary.name: Futuristic UI (FUI) / HUD Design
summary.visualIdentity: A descriptive futuristic-interface direction built from dark backgrounds, fine wireframes, and limited cyan or magenta accents with readable monospaced data. Panels, reticles, scales, maps, and progress rings must have defined functions. Startup, scanning, acquisition, and feedback animate so data changes match visible events. Avoid meaningless microtext, excessive spinning rings, and overexposed neon; label all fictional data. Not every cyberpunk scene is a HUD.
summary.suitableUses: Fictional interfaces and title sequences work well alone. Product, tech, sensor, or diagnostic explainers fit when panels carry real or clearly labeled data. Operations dashboards and mission-control style reports suit it when backed by real metrics. Interactive HTML HUD dashboards are also suitable. Suitability for other topics is inferred, not stated in the source.
summary.limitations: Dense microtext and decorative rings without data roles are discouraged. Magenta and cyan should not both appear unless the topic and restricted interface palette support it. Bloom belongs only on selected luminous elements. Oscilloscope-style CRT curvature or noise that hurts legibility should be avoided. Fictional data must be labeled. Neon overexposure is excluded. The source does not define a maximum element count or specific runtime limits.
summary.palette: Suggested tokens, not supplied exact colors: background #0C1822 as the dark layout base, foreground #E7F4F3 for text and fine strokes, and accent_1 #55C7CF as the single cyan accent. Gradients are disabled, so use discrete tokens. Approved magenta may replace cyan only as an alternative. Readable pairs: foreground on background 15.933:1; background on accent 8.942:1. Task or brand colors override these values. Verify contrast over actual composited frames, since two-color ratios do not cover video or transparency.
summary.motionAndInteraction: For video, all state derives from seekable composition time. Startup, scanning, locking, and feedback must correspond to data events. Movement should be smooth and coherent, while deliberate cuts, impacts, and reading holds stay sharp. Optional motion references include pointer-driven tilt with a neutral return, chaptered handoffs, narrative steps, and exploded reveals, each only if the scene supports it. Interactive delivery may add hover, scroll, or pointer input, with keyboard access and reduced-motion static states.
summary.audio: Audio is unspecified in the source for this style; no mandatory layer is set. Suggested options, inferred from the style, include restrained sound accents on scan, lock, and feedback events, ambience, or silence for reading holds. Music, narration, and sung vocals are optional and should not compete with speech or essential text. Any audio asset must be authorized and provided by the task. Verify intelligibility, balance, and sync in the final video.
summary.assetRequirements: Required assets are not explicitly listed for the base style. Asset needs depend on the chosen renderer: SVG or Three.js wireframes and geometry, monospaced fonts loaded locally before capture, and optional authorized map, chart, or waveform data. Chartist, Leaflet, and Cytoscape assets require the bundling, authorization, and attribution checks in their guidance. Missing assets must be reported. Prepare and cache stateful simulations before rendering.
summary.combinations: Works alone for fictional interfaces and title sequences. Hybrid pairings are suggested when the HUD must show meaningful data. style-097 supplies data panels with D3 or Leaflet charts and maps, using cyan active values with bloom on the active element only. style-063 supplies oscilloscope-style waveform traces within bounded panels in the primary cyan. Avoid off-palette accents and decorative rings without data roles.
summary.productionApproach: Use Three.js and SVG as style renderers, with UnrealBloomPass for selective bloom. Motion or GSAP owns animated properties with one owner each. HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition, timing, sync, validation, and export; Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation applies, and this must be recorded. Use chroma.js for validation and contrast. Delaunator, Cytoscape, Leaflet, Chartist, and tldraw are optional. Render delivery with the checks defined in the pipeline.
